raw:
Let me think about this push notification for a parking app.

Context: User parked at 信義停車場, timer expires in 10 minutes, overtime costs NT$60 per hour.

Need:
- s1: notification title
- s2: notification body

Constraints:
- No chatty phrasing
- No apologies, no exclamation marks
- No questions as titles
- Don't repeat title content in body
- Don't add "約" (approximately) if numbers are exact — here 10 minutes is exact
- Don't use "我們", avoid "你的/您的" unless needed
- No mainland Chinese terms (當前、設置、數據、用戶、信息 etc.)
- No periods at end of labels/buttons — though this is a notification, title/content; still keep concise
- Keep it short

Title options:
- "計時即將到期" — but which parking lot? The title could include the lot name or the body could.
- "停車計時剩餘 10 分鐘" — puts time in title, then body would repeat... body shouldn't repeat title.

Let's structure:
- s1: 信義停車場 計時即將到期
- s2: 剩餘 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60

Wait — "剩餘 10 分鐘" — is that repeating the title? Title says "計時即將到期", body says remaining 10 minutes and overtime rate. That adds new information: the time remaining and the overtime rate. That's not repetition.

Alternative:
- s1: 停車計時即將到期
- s2: 信義停車場剩餘 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60

Hmm, but including the lot name in title is more specific and useful. Actually, maybe title should be the actionable info: "計時 10 分鐘後到期"? Then body: "信義停車場，超時每小時 NT$60"。

But rule: "不要重複標題已經說過的話" — body shouldn't repeat. So split info:

Option A:
- s1: 信義停車場 計時即將到期
- s2: 剩餘 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60

Is "超時每小時 NT$60" clear? It means overtime is NT$60/hour. Maybe "超時費每小時 NT$60" is clearer. "超時每小時 NT$60" is fine and shorter.

Should there be a period at end? Rule says don't add period at end of labels and buttons. Notifications aren't exactly labels; but to be safe, no trailing period. Within body, a comma is fine.

Option B:
- s1: 停車計時剩餘 10 分鐘
- s2: 信義停車場超時每小時 NT$60

This is also concise. Title has time, body has location and rate. "停車計時剩餘 10 分鐘" — clear.

Hmm, which is better? The key urgency driver is the 10 minutes. The location may matter if user has multiple sessions. Title: "信義停車場計時即將到期" — 11 chars. Body: "剩餘 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60"。

Actually "即將到期" is a bit redundant if we say "剩餘 10 分鐘". The rule "不要解釋顯而易見的事" — "即將到期" is implied by 剩餘 10 分鐘? Not exactly, but combined they're fine.

Maybe simpler:
- s1: 信義停車場停車即將到期
- s2: 剩餘 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60

Or title: "計時快到期"? Too casual? "快" is slightly colloquial. "即將到期" is standard UI language.

Avoid "您的" — not used. Avoid "約" — 10 minutes is exact, fine.

Final:
s1: "信義停車場計時即將到期"
s2: "剩餘 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60"

Check spacing: numbers with spaces — "剩餘 10 分鐘" is fine. "NT$60" fine.

No period at end. No exclamation. No question. Good.

One more consideration: should the title be shorter, like "停車計時到期提醒"? Body then: "信義停車場剩餘 10 分鐘，超時每小時 NT$60"。That works too. "提醒" in title is okay.

I'll go with:
